what: A single motor turns a 16 mm crank. A 40 mm coupler, a 40 mm rocker and two fixed pivots 32 mm apart constrain an extended tip. The coupler continues 40 mm beyond its rocker joint. This Hoeken-type linkage gives the tip a nearly straight working stroke and an arched return. One crank drives a Hoeken-type coupler tip through a nearly straight working stroke and curved return.
try: Reset, load stride-lab.bw and Run. Follow the highlighted tip through two slow forward turns and two reverse turns.
Compare the long, nearly straight working stroke with the curved return. Watch the crank keep turning while the tip changes direction.
Watch equal intervals of time along the working stroke. Is the tip speed constant? Compare forward and reverse travel.
why: The tip follows the geometry of a closed four-bar loop. Equal 40 mm coupler and rocker lengths, a 16 mm crank, a 32 mm pivot spacing and an equal coupler extension make one half of the tip path almost straight. In ideal planar geometry, crank angles 90° to 270° give a 64 mm stroke whose vertical deviation from y = 64 mm is at most about 0.1561 mm. The motor drives the crank; it does not program the tip path.
matters: Approximate straight-line linkages can generate useful repeated working and return strokes using revolute joints, as in walking and handling mechanisms. This model illustrates the kinematics; it is not a walking robot or a load-rated machine.
question: Does a nearly straight tip path mean exact straightness or constant tip speed?
answer: No. The ideal working stroke has a small geometric deviation, and the nonlinear linkage makes tip speed vary even when crank speed is steady. Reversing the drive retraces the same ideal path in the opposite direction.
further: Compare the tip path with the crank circle and the rocker arc. All three belong to the same one-motor mechanism.
The 0.1561 mm deviation describes ideal rigid, planar geometry. It is not a prediction of real LEGO tolerances, joint play, flex or simulated tracking accuracy.
formula: A = (0, 0), D = (32, 0); B = (16 cos θ, 16 sin θ); |C − B| = |C − D| = 40; P = 2C − B [mm]. Upper branch: θ = 90°…270° gives x = 64…0 mm, y ≈ 64 mm.
